title: Alice's Adventures in Wonderland — Chapter I excerpt
author: Lewis Carroll
subject: literature
text: Alice was beginning to get very tired of sitting by her sister on the bank. She had nothing to do. Once or twice she had peeped into the book her sister was reading. The book had no pictures or conversations in it. Alice wondered whether the pleasure of making a daisy-chain would be worth the trouble of getting up and picking the daisies.

title: The North Wind and the Sun — Aesop excerpt
author: Aesop
subject: literature and moral reasoning
text: The North Wind and the Sun disputed which was the stronger. They agreed that the one who first made a traveller take off his cloak should be considered stronger. The North Wind blew with all his might, but the traveller wrapped his cloak more closely around him. The Sun then shone warmly, and the traveller soon removed his cloak.

title: On the Origin of Species — Introduction excerpt
author: Charles Darwin
subject: natural science
text: When on board H.M.S. Beagle, as naturalist, I was much struck with certain facts in the distribution of the inhabitants of South America. These facts seemed to throw some light on the origin of species. On my return home, it occurred to me that something might be made out on this question by patiently accumulating and reflecting on all sorts of facts which could possibly have any bearing on it.
